sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in New Mexico, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Tuesday, October 20Passed

Your county clerk had to receive the application by Tuesday, October 20, 2026 (14 days before the election). That deadline has passed. You can still vote early in person through Saturday, October 31, or on Election Day; you can register at an early voting site right before you vote. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be received by your county clerk, or at a voting location in your county, by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A postmark is not enough: a ballot that arrives after 7 p.m. is not counted. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Saturday, October 31, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on New Mexico’s own site

At school away from home, in New Mexico or in another state? What New Mexico says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No excuse is required. Any New Mexico voter can ask for an absentee (mailed) ballot. Voters can also join the permanent absentee list to be mailed a ballot for every statewide election. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Fill out the application online at NMVote.org. Asking online needs a New Mexico driver's license or ID issued by the state's Motor Vehicle Division; without one, use the paper application. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Download the paper application (NMAV-1), fill it out, sign it, and mail it to your county clerk so it arrives no later than 14 days before the election. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Bring a paper application to your county clerk's office, or contact the clerk's office in person, by phone, by mail or by email to get one. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the postage-paid return envelope. It must arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day, so mail it as early as you can. (official page)
  • Drop box. Put it in any official election drop box in your county. (official page)
  • In person. Drop it off at your county clerk's office or at any early voting or Election Day voting location in your county by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Only you, your caregiver, or an immediate family member (spouse, child, parent or sibling) may deliver it; that person must sign the return envelope. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Under the privacy flap of the official return envelope, sign your name and write the last four digits of your Social Security number. If either is missing, or the digits do not match your registration, the county clerk will contact you by phone, email or mail and you can fix it in person, by mail or electronically. No witness or notary is needed. If you registered for the first time by mail and did not send an ID then, you will be asked for one when you vote. (the law)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on New Mexico’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Tuesday, October 6, 2026 to Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Early voting at county clerks' offices runs from Tuesday, October 6, 2026; more early voting sites open on Saturday, October 17. Early voting ends Saturday, October 31, 2026. Check NMVote.org or your county clerk for sites and hours. (official page)

Students

At school in New Mexico, away from home

The state's pages do not speak to students separately. Its general rule is that you register where you are a New Mexico resident, and you can register as soon as you become a resident. A student ID card that shows your name and current address is one of the documents first-time voters who registered by mail can use. (official page)

At school in another state, with New Mexico as home

The state's pages do not speak to out-of-state students separately. Its general rule is that you must be a New Mexico resident to register here. A New Mexico voter can have an absentee ballot mailed to another address, but the permanent absentee list is not open to voters who want their ballot delivered to an out-of-state address, so such a voter asks for a ballot for each election. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military voters, their families and U.S. citizens overseas can register and ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application (send a new one each year) or the state's application. They can get the ballot by mail, email, fax or a secure online portal, and return it the same ways, but it must reach the county clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026. A request for a ballot by email or fax must be received by October 31, 2026. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is a backup. (official page)

New Mexico in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The last day to ask for a ballot by mail (October 20, 2026) has passed. If you already have a ballot, mail it early or drop it off; it must arrive by 7 p.m. on November 3.
  • If you asked for a mailed ballot but want to vote in person, you can, after signing a statement that you have not voted and will not vote the mailed ballot. If your ballot never came, you can vote a replacement ballot at your polling place after signing a statement that you did not receive it.
  • Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day.
  • Ballots were mailed starting October 6, 2026. The date of the email or fax request deadline for military and overseas voters (October 31) is from the FVAP guide (source 8).
